purpose: Procarbazine is a chemotherapy drug used mainly to treat Hodgkin's lymphoma, which is a type of cancer that affects the lymph nodes. It is often used in combination with other chemotherapy medicines as part of a treatment plan. In some cases, it may also be used to treat certain brain tumors.
how_it_works: Procarbazine works by getting inside cancer cells and damaging their DNA, which is like the instruction manual that tells cells how to grow and divide. When the DNA is damaged, the cancer cells can no longer copy themselves and they eventually die. This helps slow down or stop the growth of cancer in your body.
common_side_effects: Nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, feeling very tired or weak, mouth sores, trouble swallowing, hair loss, constipation or diarrhea, dizziness, and low blood cell counts (which can make you more prone to infections, bruising, or bleeding).
warnings: Procarbazine has a very important food interaction — you must avoid foods high in tyramine (like aged cheeses, cured meats, red wine, beer, and fermented foods) because combining them can cause a dangerous spike in blood pressure. You must also avoid alcohol, as it can cause a severe flushing reaction. This drug can harm an unborn baby, so reliable birth control is very important during treatment. Avoid other medications like antidepressants (especially MAOIs and SSRIs) without checking with your doctor first. You will need regular blood tests to monitor your blood cell counts.
typical_dosing: Dosing is determined by your doctor based on your body size and overall health. A common starting dose is around 2 to 4 mg per kilogram of body weight per day, taken by mouth, often in divided doses. Your doctor will adjust this based on how your body responds and your blood test results. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never change your dose on your own.
